title: Houses Torched in Deserted Kuki Village in Manipur's Kamjong District
excerpt: Suspected militants set fire to homes in Khoikai village near Chassad early on Wednesday; no casualties were reported as residents had already fled amid worsening Kuki-Naga clashes.
body:
• Suspected militants set fire to several houses in Khoikai, a deserted Kuki village near Chassad in Manipur's Kamjong district, at about 5:30 a.m. on Wednesday, police said.
  • No casualties were reported because the village's residents had already fled as clashes between the Kuki and Naga communities worsened.
  • The arson came four days after at least 15 houses were burnt in neighbouring Chassad village, hours after a Kuki civilian was shot dead and four others were injured there.
  • Police said the extent of the damage and the identity of those behind Wednesday's arson were yet to be established.

Suspected militants set fire to several houses in Khoikai, a deserted Kuki village in Manipur's Kamjong district, early on Wednesday, police said, in the latest attack in a district that has seen a string of violent incidents over the past few days. The village, near Chassad, was set ablaze at around 5:30 a.m., according to a report by DY365. Its residents had fled earlier, as clashes between the Kuki and Naga communities worsened.

Police said the extent of the damage and the identity of those behind the arson were yet to be established. No casualties were reported, as nobody lives in the village.

Four days after Chassad burned

Wednesday's arson came barely four days after at least 15 houses were burnt in neighbouring Chassad village late on Saturday, hours after a Kuki civilian was shot dead and four others were injured, officials said. Scores of residents fled to nearby forests and an Army camp after that attack. A joint column of the Assam Rifles, the BSF and Kamjong Police was deployed in the area.

Deputy Chief Minister Nemcha Kipgen condemned the Chassad attack and called the burning of homes an "intolerable crime." On the same night, three Tangkhul Naga civilians suffered bullet injuries in an attack at the Kamjong district headquarters, officials said.

A year of Kuki-Naga violence

More than 50 people have been killed and dozens of houses burnt in Kuki-Naga violence since the beginning of the year, with Tamenglong, Noney, Kangpokpi, Ukhrul and Kamjong among the affected districts, according to the DY365 report. Kamjong, which borders Myanmar, has been among the most volatile of those districts in recent days, with attacks moving between villages and the district headquarters.

The pattern in Khoikai underlines why the toll keeps rising even when no one is killed. The village had already been emptied by fear before the attackers arrived, so the arson destroyed homes and property rather than lives. Each such attack makes return harder for the families who fled, and deepens the displacement that has defined Manipur's ethnic conflict.

Tension in the Imphal valley

The situation in the Imphal valley has also been tense since Monday, when suspected militants opened fire on a group of Meitei villagers who had gone to collect firewood at Sunulok hill, on the Imphal East-Kangpokpi border. Three of them were killed and three injured, police said.

Addressing the media on Tuesday, Additional Director General of Police Lhatoo said three people had been arrested during search operations by Manipur Police, the CRPF and CoBRA in villages under Sagolmang police station. Two of them had admitted to being part of the assault team during preliminary questioning, he said, while the role of the third was being examined. Police said 12 firearms, including an INSAS rifle, an M16, an AK-47 and a sniper rifle, were recovered on the basis of the accused's disclosures, along with 1,095 rounds of ammunition and a quantity of explosives.

What to watch

Police have yet to name those responsible for the Khoikai arson or quantify the damage, and no official statement on Wednesday's attack had been reported at the time of the DY365 report. Whether security forces extend the joint deployments used after the Chassad attack to the villages around Khoikai, and whether displaced residents receive protection to return, will determine whether Kamjong's week of violence continues to spread from village to village.
